correctness.rationale: The free-center event is the triple intersection of caps around the data points; antipodal reflection gives the complementary large-cap coverage event, up to the null boundary. For uniform samples, the lens of possible centers for the first two points dilated by ε gives the third-point region. Its spherical Steiner area is 2π−2cos(ε)γ−4cos(2ε)β; the two angular integrals are π(1−cos ε) and π sin²ε, giving the known F_0 and ε⁶ coefficient −1/4. In exponential coordinates the offsets have norm at most 2, and the possible center is within scaled distance 1 of the anchor. Uniform convergence of scaled distances on this compact set gives convergence of the event indicator except at planar enclosing radius 1, a null level by radial homogeneity in R⁴. For a planar anchor separation r, the allowed third-point area is 6 arccos(r/2)−(r/2)√(4−r²)+π. Its integrals against 2πr and 2πr³ give 9π² and T=15π², respectively. Swapping and reanchoring give isotropic second moment matrices T/2 for each offset and cross moment T/4. Rotation by π at the anchor cancels the first-order term exactly. Uniform C² Taylor remainders on the compact scaled domain and dominated convergence then give (T/2)∫ f²Δf+(T/4)D_3=−(3T/4)D_3 for the second-order density term. The anchor-independent constant-density kernel mass is exactly 16π²F_0/ε⁴, contributing −4π² I_3 to the sixth-order coefficient without differentiating a nonsmooth cluster boundary. The normalized leading kernel factors as the f³-weighted anchor law times the uniform law on the offset set. Positivity of f and connectedness give the stated rigidity. The ε=π/2 endpoint of the uniform formula follows by continuity; it is not needed for the expansion.
residual_risks: Frozen quadratures were inspected, not executed. Independent moment and Legendre coefficient checks are finite consistency checks, not a proof for general f. The error is for a fixed C² density and does not assert uniformity over a varying density class.
